mcqs.q: In a HQHVSN ovariohysterectomy trial, which suture allowed faster three-layer continuous incisional closure?
mcqs.e: Barbed suture averaged 4.91 min vs 6.5 min for smooth monofilament.

mcqs.q: Besides suture method, what was significantly associated with closure time?
mcqs.e: Each additional cm of incision added ~39 s; BCS and weight were not significant.

mcqs.q: What was the short-term complication finding between the two suture types?
mcqs.e: No short-term telemedicine-assessed complications were noted with either method.

mcqs.q: What is the treatment of choice for canine pyometra?
mcqs.e: OVH, often with perioperative antimicrobials, is definitive.

mcqs.q: What did outcomes suggest about antibiotic susceptibility after OVH for pyometra?
o: Recovery required a fully susceptible antibiotic
Good recovery occurred even with non-susceptible antibiotics
All bitches relapsed without susceptibility-guided therapy
mcqs.e: All animals recovered well even though 30% never received a fully effective antibiotic by MIC.

mcqs.q: Which organism was most frequently isolated, and the suggested best option?
mcqs.e: E. coli was most common; cephazolin was the best option for it.

journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery

mcqs.q: Which PDX suture size could NOT be recommended for feline ventral midline closure?
mcqs.e: 5-0 PDX failed by suture breakage in 6/8 samples.

mcqs.q: Which sizes can be used without reservation for cat coeliotomy closure?
mcqs.e: PDX 2-0 and 3-0 were recommended without reservation; 4-0 with caution.

mcqs.q: How did suture-material failure risk relate to suture diameter?
o: Only the abdominal wall failed regardless
mcqs.e: Risk of suture material failure increased as diameter decreased.

journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery

mcqs.q: Comparing midline vs flank ovariectomy in feral cats, which was true of the flank approach?
o: Smaller incision and shorter surgery time
mcqs.e: Midline had larger incisions and longer surgery; flank was smaller and faster.

mcqs.q: What was the difference in intraoperative nociception between approaches?
mcqs.e: No significant nociception difference was detected between approaches.

mcqs.q: Why might the flank approach be favored in sterilisation programmes?
o: Smaller incision reduces dehiscence risk when postop control is difficult
mcqs.e: Smaller incisions allow more animals done and lower dehiscence risk where wound control is impossible.

mcqs.q: What was the most frequently cited reason for not using the feline ovarian pedicle tie?
mcqs.e: Non-use was most attributed to absence of the technique from vet school training.

mcqs.q: What proportion of survey respondents reported using the pedicle tie?
mcqs.e: 77 of 142 respondents used it, over half.

mcqs.q: Among non-users, what was the predominant view on whether the pedicle tie meets standard of care?
o: All said it never meets SOC
mcqs.e: Of non-users, 60% said it meets SOC, 14% no, 26% sometimes.

authors: De Oliveira Sampaio, Keytyanne, et al.
journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery

mcqs.q: Which group of male cats had the earliest onset of urethral obstruction?
mcqs.e: Intact cats obstructed earlier (3.6 yr) than neutered groups (5.5-5.7 yr).

mcqs.q: How did age at neutering affect onset of urethral obstruction?
o: No effect; intact had earliest onset regardless
mcqs.e: Intact cats had earliest onset regardless of age at neutering.

mcqs.q: How did clinical signs and histopathologic lesions compare across groups?
mcqs.e: Signs (stranguria, hematuria) and lesions were similar in all groups.

mcqs.q: What did this retrospective study find about pediatric neutering and later health conditions?
o: No statistically significant association with the conditions studied
mcqs.e: No significant link was found between neuter age and obesity, behavior, urinary, or joint disease.

mcqs.q: How were outcome data collected in this study?
mcqs.e: Data came from a telephone questionnaire to 105 owners of shelter-adopted animals.

mcqs.q: Which behavior occurred most frequently in intact male dogs?
mcqs.e: Urine marking occurred in 78% of intact males, the highest rate.

mcqs.q: What was found for intact vs desexed female dogs across the three behaviors?
o: No differences for any of the three behaviors
mcqs.e: No differences were seen between intact and desexed females for marking, mounting, or roaming.

mcqs.q: How did mounting and roaming change with age in intact males?
mcqs.e: Both behaviors were less frequent in older intact males, suggesting decline with age.

mcqs.q: What did earlier neutering, especially in female kittens, do to body composition?
mcqs.e: Earlier neutering produced a more marked upward growth trajectory and greater fat mass, especially in females.

mcqs.q: By 52 weeks, how did neutered kittens compare with intact controls?
o: Heavier with greater fat and lean mass
mcqs.e: Neutered cats were heavier with greater fat and lean mass and larger abdominal girth.

mcqs.q: For which neutering timing was the upward growth inclination least marked?
mcqs.e: The upward inclination was least in kittens neutered after 28-29 weeks.

mcqs.q: Which breed showed no significant effect of early neutering on joint disorders or cancers?
mcqs.e: Siberian Huskies showed no significant joint or cancer effects from early neutering.

mcqs.q: What is the study's overarching recommendation about neutering age?
o: Personalized decisions by breed, sex, and context
mcqs.e: Results emphasize personalized neutering decisions considering breed, sex, and context.

mcqs.q: Joint disorder risk with early neutering was heightened in which dogs?
o: Larger breeds and mixed-breeds over 20 kg
mcqs.e: Risks were heightened for some larger breeds and mixed-breed dogs over 20 kg.

mcqs.q: What were the odds of early-onset urinary incontinence in bitches neutered later vs early?
mcqs.e: Later-age neutering carried 0.80 times the odds of early-onset UI.

mcqs.q: What is the practical recommendation from this study?
o: Delay neutering until after 7 months unless justified otherwise
mcqs.e: Preference should be given to delaying neutering until after 7 months unless major reasons justify earlier surgery.

mcqs.q: Which methodology did this study apply to observational VetCompass data?
mcqs.e: It used the target trial emulation framework for causal inference.

mcqs.q: What did this scoping review conclude about evidence on neutering timing relative to puberty?
o: Robust evidence does not yet exist
mcqs.e: Robust evidence to guide timing relative to puberty does not yet exist.

mcqs.q: For which outcomes were NO studies found examining pre- vs post-pubertal neutering?
o: Atopy, developmental orthopaedic disease, and obesity
mcqs.e: No studies examined pre/post-pubertal neutering effects on atopy, DOD, or obesity.
